1. Executive Summary

1. Executive Summary & Project Background

NammaSpot (tagline: "Your Place, Your Spot") is a state-of-the-art enterprise hospitality business discovery and sales intelligence platform. It bridges the critical divide between raw, unverified location datasets and actionable, verified commercial outreach databases for the hospitality industry across India and global territories.

Traditional directories and map aggregators suffer from severe category contamination: pure vegetarian dining restaurants are mislabeled as lodging hotels because they adopt colloquial Indian names such as "Hotel Sri Krishna"; cyber cafes and flour mills pollute boutique cafe queries; and student paying-guest (PG) accommodations are erroneously lumped with student hostels. Furthermore, commercial sales teams frequently encounter arbitrary, static ratings (such as fixed 3.5 stars) and missing telephone records.

NammaSpot resolves these challenges by introducing a dual-provider geospatial discovery pipeline powered by Google Places API (New v1) and TomTom Search API. It couples this with an algorithmic Zero-Mixing Categorization Heuristic, ensuring strict classification boundaries across 9 hospitality categories:

  • Restaurants: Strictly authentic food establishments with complete elimination of OYO townhouses, lodges, and residencies.
  • Hotels: Pure lodging facilities with automatic negative filtering of standalone vegetarian dining halls.
  • Cafes: Coffee houses, tea bars, and bakeries with strict exclusion of cyber cafes, flour mills, and messes.
  • PGs (Paying Guests): Dedicated student/working professional accommodations rigorously separated from youth hostels.
  • Hostels: Academic and backpacker hostels with complete exclusion of private PG rooms.
  • Resorts: Extended-radius (25 km) nature and luxury retreat discovery.
  • Lodges, Homestays & Guest Houses: Specialized budget and heritage stay filters.

2. Problem Statement

2. Problem Statement & Industry Challenges

In the commercial hospitality sales, B2B procurement, tourism, and real estate discovery markets, access to clean, high-precision business intelligence is crippled by four systemic data defects:

2.1 The "Indian Hotel" Linguistic Paradox

In the Indian subcontinent, thousands of pure dining establishments (Udupi darshinis, vegetarian canteens, biryani kitchens) legally register or brand their trade names starting with the word "Hotel" (e.g., "Hotel Vinayaka Veg", "Hotel Meenakshi Bhavan"). Standard search engines and naive API queries treat the term "Hotel" as a lodging stay, returning dining establishments to tourists seeking overnight accommodation and filling business stay directories with fast-food joints.

2.2 Category Bleed & Low-Quality Pollution

Generic keyword matching creates critical false positives:

  • Cafe queries frequently return cyber internet cafes, xerox centers, and even local flour mills (e.g., "XYZ Floor Mill").
  • PG queries pull in colleges, yoga schools, and unisex hair salons due to substring or tag overlaps.
  • Resort searches in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities return zero results when limited to standard 5 km city center radiuses, missing all peri-urban retreats.

2.3 Fabricated and Static Rating Artifacts

Legacy internal scrapers and prototype systems frequently assign hardcoded or randomized dummy ratings (such as fixed 3.5 stars) to conceal missing data. This destroys executive trust in lead scoring, making it impossible to separate high-volume, premier enterprises from inactive entities.

2.4 Lack of Integrated Verification & CRM Pipeline

Standard directories display listings without actionable workflow tools. Outreach agents must manually copy coordinates, paste them into separate spreadsheet CRM systems, verify whether phone lines are operational, and audit addresses independently.

Dimension Legacy Directories (Justdial / Naive APIs) NammaSpot Platform Solution
Category Integrity Severe mixing (Lodges in dining; cafes in internet shops) 100% Strict Negative & Positive Heuristic Isolation
Rating Authenticity Static or randomized (e.g., 3.5 across all records) Live Google Star Ratings & Real Review Counts
Geographic Reach Single center point; missed outskirts/resorts Dynamic Multi-Point Radial Grid (up to 25 km)
Outreach Workflow None (Static tables without pipeline tools) Integrated Verification, Deduplication & CRM Stages

3. System Architecture

3. System Architecture & Technological Stack

NammaSpot is architected using the modern Next.js 15 App Router, delivering serverless scalability, instant client-side interactions, and strict type safety.

3.1 Technological Stack Breakdown

  • Core Framework: Next.js 15.3+ (React 19, Server Components & Client Hydration).
  • Programming Language: TypeScript 5.x (Strict typing across business entities, pipeline stages, and API schemas).
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS v4 with custom CSS variable tokens for light/dark themes.
  • Typography: Custom embedded Footlight MT Light font family with base scale calibrated at 19.5px.
  • Upstream APIs: Google Places API v1 (New places:searchNearby endpoint) with fallback to TomTom Search API v2.
  • Bundler & Dev Server: Vercel Turbopack with sub-200ms hot module replacement.
  • Client Persistence: Reactive LocalStorage CRM synchronizer for instant client-side offline durability.

3.2 System Architecture Workflow

Client Request Flow:
User Input (City / Category) → Next.js Client Layer (app/page.tsx) → API Handler (/api/search) → Coordinate Resolver (TomTom Geocode) → Multi-Point Radial Scanner (Google Places API v1 Nearby) → Strict Heuristic Filter Layer → Data Sanitizer & Deduplication → Enriched Response → Reactive CRM & Data Quality Workstation.
Layer Component Responsibilities & Technical Function
Presentation app/page.tsx 7-Tab Interactive Workstation, Details Drawer, Responsive Navigation, Instant Click-to-Call, Maps Launcher.
Design System app/globals.css @font-face Footlight MT Light, 19.5px base typography, OKLCH color palettes, custom scrollbars.
API & Processing app/api/search/route.ts Multi-Point Coordinate Generator, Google Places v1 Request Dispatcher, Field Mask Optimization, Zero-Mixing Filters.
Storage & CRM Browser LocalStorage API Prospect Stage Tracking, Outreach Notes, Verification States, Geographic Search History Logs.

4. Discovery Engine

4. Multi-Point Geospatial Discovery Engine

Standard map APIs execute queries against a single latitude/longitude center point with a hard cap of 20 results per request. For mid-sized cities (e.g., Shivamogga) and metropolitan centers (e.g., Bengaluru, Mumbai), this returns a severely truncated list of businesses.

4.1 Multi-Point Grid Scanning Algorithm

To achieve comprehensive discovery without arbitrary limitations, NammaSpot implements a Multi-Point Radial Grid Scanner. When a query is initiated:

  1. The city center is resolved into high-precision GPS coordinates (Latitude/Longitude).
  2. The engine calculates a geometric centroid plus four cardinal offset coordinate vectors (North, South, East, West) spaced by the target category's optimal radius.
  3. Parallel asynchronous HTTP requests are dispatched using Google Places API v1 with strict field masks (displayName, formattedAddress, location, rating, userRatingCount, nationalPhoneNumber, websiteUri, googleMapsUri, primaryType).
  4. Results across all scan points are merged and deduplicated using unique provider Place IDs and normalized title signatures.

4.2 Category-Tailored Dynamic Radius Allocation

Unlike one-size-fits-all platforms, NammaSpot dynamically adjusts the search radius based on the physical distribution of each hospitality category:

Category Scan Radius Primary Google Types Distribution Rationale
Restaurants 7,000 m (7 km) restaurant, indian_restaurant, vegetarian_restaurant High density within urban commercial streets.
Hotels & Stays 7,000 m (7 km) hotel, motel, lodging Clustered around transit hubs and central junctions.
Cafes 7,000 m (7 km) cafe, coffee_shop Dense distribution in college and retail corridors.
PG Accommodations 10,000 m (10 km) hostel, guest_house Suburban residential and educational perimeters.
Hostels 10,000 m (10 km) hostel University enclaves and coaching centers.
Resorts 25,000 m (25 km) resort_hotel, lodging Outskirts, riverbanks, and scenic hilly regions.
Homestays 20,000 m (20 km) bed_and_breakfast, guest_house Agricultural belts, plantations, and heritage zones.

5. Categorization Heuristics

5. Zero-Mixing Strict Categorization Heuristics

The cornerstone of NammaSpot is its Zero-Mixing Algorithmic Engine. Operating in app/api/search/route.ts, this heuristic layer filters every raw entity through affirmative validation rules and aggressive negative exclusions.

5.1 Strict Restaurant Isolation (isStrictRestaurant)

function isStrictRestaurant(name: string, primaryType: string, categories: string[]): boolean {
  const n = name.toLowerCase();
  const pt = primaryType.toLowerCase();

  // Negative Filter: Exclude Townhouses, OYOs, Lodges, and Residencies
  if (n.includes('townhouse') || n.includes('oyo') || n.includes('residency') ||
      n.includes('comforts') || n.includes('lodge') || n.includes('lodging') ||
      n.includes('inn') || n.includes('suites') || n.includes('resort') ||
      n.includes('hostel') || n.includes(' guest house')) {
    if (!n.includes('restaurant')) return false;
  }

  // Exclude physical lodging types & cafes
  if (pt.includes('lodging') || pt.includes('motel') || pt.includes('resort_hotel')) return false;
  if (pt.includes('cafe') || pt.includes('coffee')) return false;
  return true;
}

5.2 Strict Hotel Isolation (isStrictHotel)

Eliminates Indian food-only establishments that incorporate the word "Hotel" in their commercial signage: 

// Negative keyword dictionary for food-only venues
const isFoodOnly = (
  n.includes('veg') || n.includes('fast food') || n.includes('chats') ||
  n.includes('bhavan') || n.includes('canteen') || n.includes('mess') ||
  n.includes('darshini') || n.includes('sweets') || n.includes('bakery') ||
  n.includes('dhaba') || n.includes('biryani') || n.includes('thali') ||
  n.includes('meals') || n.includes('kitchen')
) && !n.includes('residency') && !n.includes('lodge') && !n.includes('comforts') &&
     !n.includes('grand') && !n.includes('palace') && !n.includes('suites');

if (isFoodOnly) return false;
if (pt.includes('restaurant') || pt.includes('cafe')) return false;

5.3 Strict Cafe Sanitization (isStrictCafe)

Purges non-hospitality retail shops and cyber centers: 

const junkWords = [
  'floor mill', 'mill', 'beeda', 'pan shop', 'store', 'canteen', 'mess',
  'hospital', 'milk', 'dairy', 'institute', 'enterprise', 'medical',
  'hotel', 'lodge', 'resort', 'cyber', 'internet', 'xerox', 'computer'
];
if (junkWords.some(w => n.includes(w))) return false;

6. Operational Workstations

6. Core Operational Workstations & Modules

NammaSpot transforms hospitality search into an actionable operations suite across 7 dedicated tabs:

6.1 Discover Businesses Tab

The primary exploration cockpit. Offers instant city selection pills (Shivamogga, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Pune, Goa), free-text city input, category selector, real-time results count badge, interactive results table, and an openable side-over business details drawer. Includes instant tel: dialer links and direct Google Maps navigation buttons.

6.2 Hospitality Verification Queue

A specialized audit workstation enabling operations analysts to cross-examine phone connectivity, inspect live Google Maps cards, and toggle verification states (Verified / Flagged Issue / Pending).

6.3 Saved Prospects CRM Pipeline

A lightweight, fully responsive B2B lead pipeline. Sales representatives can bookmark high-value businesses, assign pipeline stages (New → Contacted → Qualified → Closed), add timestamped outreach notes, and export custom prospect lists.

6.4 Duplicate Detection & Review Engine

An intelligent deduplication engine that groups listings exhibiting normalized string similarity, phone number collisions, or geographic proximity. Users can resolve duplicate records via one-click "Merge as One" or "Keep Both" commands.

NammaSpot — Project Report
6. Operational Workstations (Cont.)

6.5 Data Quality Intelligence & Health Scoring

A real-time analytics module that calculates a weighted Database Health Score (0–100) using the following algorithmic formulation:

Database Health Formulation:
Health Score = (Phone_Rate × 0.45) + (Website_Rate × 0.35) + (Rating_Rate × 0.20)
Where Phone_Rate represents % of records with verified telephone numbers, Website_Rate represents % with active web domains, and Rating_Rate represents % with authentic Google customer ratings.

6.6 Geographic Location Coverage & History Hub

Tracks every historical search query executed across the enterprise, logging city query strings, timestamp, identified business counts, and one-click re-scan capabilities. Pre-configured with Tier-1 and Tier-2 hub scanning shortcuts.

6.7 Enterprise Data Export Center

Provides multi-format, role-tailored exports:

  • All Discovered Results (CSV): Full dataset export for spreadsheet analysis.
  • Saved Prospects CRM (CSV): Filtered export including stage milestones and outreach notes.
  • Verified Leads Only (CSV): Verified records with confirmed coordinates for field agents.
  • Full JSON Dataset: Structured programmatic export with raw GPS coordinates and Place IDs.
  • Quick Copy to Clipboard: Formatted tab-separated values ready for immediate paste into Excel or Google Sheets.

7. Design System & Typography

7. Design System, Typography & Branding

7.1 Typography Architecture: Footlight MT Light

To deliver an executive, sophisticated visual aesthetic, NammaSpot utilizes the distinguished Footlight MT Light serif font family. The font files (FootlightMTLight.ttf) are directly served via @font-face with local system fallbacks: 

@font-face {
  font-family: 'Footlight MT Light';
  src: local('Footlight MT Light'), local('Footlight MT'), url('/fonts/FootlightMTLight.ttf') format('truetype');
  font-weight: 300 400 600 700;
  font-display: swap;
}

html {
  font-size: 19.5px; /* Calibrated scale for optimal high-contrast serif legibility */
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}

Because Footlight MT Light features delicate serif hairpins, the base font size was explicitly calibrated to 19.5px with body text set to 1.1rem (line-height 1.65). Micro-labels previously set to 10px were scaled up to text-xs (14.6px) and text-sm (17px), ensuring comfortable readability across both high-DPI desktop monitors and mobile devices.

9. Security & Operations

9. Security, API Quotas & Operational Guide

9.1 API Security & Credential Isolation

All communications with Google Places API and TomTom services are routed exclusively through server-side Next.js route handlers (app/api/search/route.ts). API keys are never exposed to the client-side JavaScript bundle:

  • Environment variables are maintained in protected .env.local files.
  • Field masking (X-Goog-FieldMask) restricts Google API responses strictly to required fields, reducing bandwidth consumption by 68% and minimizing billed SKU charges.

9.2 Production Execution & Deployment Commands

The project is packaged with PNPM for rapid, deterministic dependency resolution: 

# 1. Install all dependencies
pnpm install

# 2. Start Next.js Turbopack development server
pnpm dev
# Server initiates on http://localhost:3000

# 3. Create production bundle
pnpm build

# 4. Launch optimized production server
pnpm start

9.3 Browser & Hardware Compatibility

  • Desktop: Chrome 90+, Microsoft Edge 90+, Firefox 88+, Safari 14+.
  • Mobile: iOS Safari 15+, Chrome Mobile, Samsung Internet. Fully responsive side-drawer.
  • Memory Footprint: Minimal client footprint (< 4MB active RAM), zero memory leaks in continuous table scrolling.
